findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is essentially zero and slightly on the wrong side: -0.13 % short-direction excess per case over 5 days, t -0.29, on 617 cases. On my own 5-day grid it is -0.16 %, t -0.22, on 272 cases, and no horizon from 1 to 20 days gets past |t| 1.34 (10 days: +1.03 %, t 0.93, 137 cases).
findings.F2: The effect is mixed across coins and years, and the coins pull in opposite directions. Over 5 days BTC shows +1.74 % (t 1.92, 57 cases), XRP +1.51 % and XMR +1.10 %. ETH shows -1.80 %, LTC -1.41 % and ZEC -2.74 %. By year, 2019 shows +3.89 % (t 2.46, 30 cases) while 2020 shows -2.32 % (t -1.93, 56 cases).
findings.F3: A deeper failure does not lead to a larger fall. Against the raw depth below the old high, the Spearman rank correlation is 0.005 over 5 days (p 0.93, 272 cases) and 0.100 over 10 days (p 0.25). By depth tercile the 5-day excess is -0.15 % for the shallowest, -0.72 % for the middle and +0.39 % for the deepest.
findings.F4: Failed breakouts are often followed by a fresh attempt higher, which the brief names as a way the theory fails: 48.5 % of the 235 failures closed above the breakout bar's close within the next 10 days.
findings.F5: The effect shows only when the coin's 20-day volatility of daily returns is low, and it reverses when volatility is high. In the low-volatility tercile the 5-day short return is +2.23 % (t 2.54, 78 cases). It is -1.72 % in the middle tercile (t -1.55) and -3.31 % in the high tercile (t -1.91). The Spearman rank correlation between volatility and the 5-day short return is -0.161 (p 0.013, 235 cases).
findings.F6: A failed breakout predicts no more decline than an ordinary down day. Over 5 days, down days outside the situation give +0.53 % short-direction excess (t 1.93, 1,502 cases), against -0.16 % after failures.

ideas.idea: When a coin's daily close moves above its prior 20-day high and then, within the next 3 days, closes back below that old high, the coin falls over the next 5 days, only while the coin's 20-day volatility of daily returns is low, and the lower that volatility, the larger the fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader would short a failed breakout in a calm market and refuse the short when the coin has been swinging widely, because there failures tend to recover.
ideas.name: calm-market failed breakout decline
